name: Gamaredon
description: Gamaredon is an FSB-linked espionage group operating out of Russian-occupied Crimea, conducting near-continuous, high-tempo spearphishing campaigns almost exclusively against Ukrainian government, military, and law enforcement targets. Despite relatively low technical sophistication, the group compensates through sheer volume — sending waves of phishing emails roughly monthly since at least September 2025 — and rapid, incremental malware mutation to evade signature-based detection. In 2025-2026 the group escalated activity against Western military missions operating in Ukraine, using infected removable drives and an updated GammaSteel infostealer, and began exploiting CVE-2025-8088 (a WinRAR path-traversal flaw) via HTML-smuggled RAR/ARJ archives delivered through weaponized XHTML lures. Recent payload evolution moved from HTA droppers to VBScript (.vbs) and obfuscated VBScript (.vbe) files by spring 2026, alongside Supabase-hosted tracking pixels to confirm lure execution. Gamaredon remains one of the most prolific and persistent threats to Ukrainian networks, supporting Russian military intelligence collection and lateral propagation into allied/partner networks.

ttps.notes: Monthly waves of spearphishing emails with weaponized XHTML/HTA/VBScript attachments sent from compromised local government accounts
Continuous, incremental obfuscation and code mutation of Pteranodon/PteroLNK loaders to evade signature detection
USB worm propagation used to breach air-gapped systems and Western military mission networks
HTML smuggling via XHTML lures delivers RAR/ARJ archives exploiting CVE-2025-8088 (WinRAR path traversal)
Telegram, Telegraph, and other legitimate web services used as dead-drop resolvers for C2 infrastructure
Fast-flux DNS and short-lived dynamic DNS domains rotated rapidly across thousands of subdomains
Pteranodon module periodically captures screenshots of victim desktops for exfiltration
GammaSteel infostealer exfiltrates documents and credentials over the established C2 channel

notable_techniques: Operates at extremely high tempo, launching new spearphishing waves on roughly a monthly cadence with minimal pauses
Sender and recipient addresses on phishing emails are identical, with real targets hidden in the BCC field
Uses Supabase-hosted tracking endpoints embedded in XHTML lures to confirm when a victim opens the document
Shifted from a single-binary architecture to a modular multi-payload chain between 2023 and 2025
Spoofs bot-like user-agent strings (e.g., Bingbot) in C2 traffic to blend in with legitimate web crawler activity
Mimics encoded VBScript (.vbe) extensions to slip past extension-based mail filtering
Heavy reliance on dynamic DNS and fast-flux infrastructure makes domain-based blocking largely ineffective
detection_opportunities: Alert on inbound emails where the sender and 'To' address are identical and recipients appear only in BCC
Monitor for WinRAR/7-Zip extraction paths that traverse outside the intended directory (CVE-2025-8088 indicators)
Flag execution of .hta, .vbs, and .vbe files originating from email attachments or removable media
Detect autorun/LNK file creation events on USB removable drives, especially on government endpoints
Hunt for outbound HTTP requests to Telegram/Telegraph APIs or Supabase endpoints from non-developer workstations
Monitor DNS for high-volume queries to newly registered or short-TTL dynamic DNS domains
Inspect User-Agent strings claiming to be search engine crawlers (Bingbot, Googlebot) originating from internal hosts
response_playbook: Flag inbound emails where the sender and 'To' address are identical, with real recipients hidden in BCC.
Block or flag execution of .hta, .vbs, and .vbe files originating from email attachments or removable media.
Hunt for outbound requests to Telegram/Telegraph/Supabase endpoints from non-developer workstations.
Monitor DNS for high-volume queries to newly registered or short-TTL dynamic DNS domains.
Inspect WinRAR/7-Zip extraction paths for directory traversal (CVE-2025-8088 indicators).
Given this actor's roughly monthly campaign cadence, treat any single detection as likely part of a broader active wave and expand the hunting window.
